intended_object: The standard bijection, over a local ring R, between the R-points of the projective Weierstrass model (sections of Proj R[X,Y,Z]/(F) → Spec R) and the projective classes [X:Y:Z] of solutions of the projective Weierstrass equation with unimodular coordinates. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The domain is the set of sections g of `projModelOver W : projModel W ⟶ Spec R`, i.e. g ≫ π = 𝟙. The codomain is the set of projective point classes (triples up to multiplication by units) that satisfy `UnimodularLift`, meaning a representative solves the projective Weierstrass equation and has coordinates generating the unit ideal. This condition does not depend on the choice of representative. The map is the inverse of `sectionOfClass`, which sends a representative with a unit coordinate Pᵢ to the point on the chart D₊(Xᵢ) with Xₖ/Xᵢ = Pₖ/Pᵢ. The library proves that `sectionOfClass` is bijective. This is the usual description of E(R) for a local ring R, with no ellipticity assumed.

The local-ring hypothesis belongs to the content of the statement. Over a general ring, a section corresponds to a line bundle L with a surjection O³ → L, and it comes from a unimodular triple only when L is trivial. So the bijection really needs R local (or at least trivial Picard data), and that is the standard setting for this result.

Mathlib has no counterpart. It has the Weierstrass equations and the projective point classes, but not the scheme-theoretic model or its points.
